key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow maps free-energy stability across hybrid perovskite alloy compositions, showing that stable regions are narrower in Sn-based alloys than in Pb-based ones and are favored by high iodide content.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a practical composition guide for designing more thermodynamically stable mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskites for solar cells.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials were trained on DFT data to rapidly relax alloy structures.
A secondary ML model predicted energies directly from unrelaxed structures.
Free-energy landscapes were computed across composition and phase space, including alloy disorder and FA molecular orientations.
evidence_signal: The models were used to evaluate phase stability across the full (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 composition spaces, revealing composition-dependent stability trends rather than a center-of-space stabilization.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on ML surrogates trained on DFT data, its predictions may be sensitive to training coverage and may require retraining for new chemistries or phases.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
